correctness.rationale: For \(t_{j,n}=\|w_{j,n}\|_Y\), the source's norm-one \(f_j\) gives \(r_n\le t_{j,n}\le1\), so normalized elementary tensors \(v_{j,n}\) satisfy \(\varphi(v_{j,n})=r_n/t_{j,n}\to1\). The auxiliary functionals \(g_1=\frac43f_1+\frac23f_2\), \(g_2=-\frac23f_1-\frac43f_2\), and \(g_3=-\frac23f_1+\frac23f_2\) have norm exactly \(1\) on the actual generators of \(B_Y\) and are compatible with \(x_1+x_2+x_3=0\), hence define a norm-one \(C:X\to Y^*\). Its bilinear functional gives \(\|v_{1,n}-v_{2,n}\|_\pi\ge r_n(1/t_{1,n}+1/t_{2,n})\ge2r_n\to2\), while the unit-ball diameter is at most \(2\). The symmetric claim follows because the published \(J\) is isometric and \(\Psi(Jv)=\varphi(v)\). No experimental approximation is used.
